variants.question: What is deflation?
choices: A sustained fall in the general price level
variants.explanation: Deflation is the opposite of inflation.

variants.question: Which index is most commonly used to measure consumer price inflation?
variants.explanation: The consumer price index tracks the cost of a basket of goods and services.

variants.question: Which treaty, signed in 1992, created the European Union?
variants.explanation: The Treaty on European Union took effect in 1993.

variants.question: In which year did euro banknotes and coins enter circulation?
variants.explanation: The euro existed as an accounting currency from 1999 and as cash from 2002.

variants.question: How long is the term of the President of the French Republic?
variants.explanation: The term was cut from seven to five years by a 2000 referendum.

variants.question: Under which republic, founded in 1958, does France currently operate?
variants.explanation: The Fifth Republic's constitution was drafted under Charles de Gaulle.

variants.question: What does the abbreviation GDP stand for?
variants.explanation: GDP means gross domestic product.

variants.question: GDP per capita is GDP divided by what?
variants.explanation: It gives the average output per person.

variants.question: What is the right to vote called?
variants.explanation: Universal suffrage means every adult citizen may vote.

variants.question: How many rounds does a French presidential election have at most?
variants.explanation: If no candidate wins an absolute majority in the first round, the top two meet in a second round.

variants.question: In which city is the headquarters of the United Nations?
variants.explanation: The UN headquarters stands in Manhattan.

variants.question: Which of these countries is NOT a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
variants.explanation: Germany sits on the Council only when elected as a non-permanent member.

variants.question: In which city does the French National Assembly sit?
variants.explanation: The deputies meet at the Palais Bourbon in Paris.

variants.question: Which body reviews whether French laws conform to the Constitution?
variants.explanation: The Conseil constitutionnel is the French constitutional authority.

variants.question: After whom is the Napoleonic Code named?
variants.explanation: Napoleon pushed through the codification as First Consul.

variants.question: Which principle did the 1804 Code civil affirm?
choices: Equality before the law and the protection of property
variants.explanation: The Code ended feudal privileges and confirmed property rights.

variants.question: Adam Smith is considered a founder of which field?
variants.explanation: He is often called the father of modern economics.

variants.question: In which year was The Wealth of Nations published?
variants.explanation: It appeared in 1776, the year of the American Declaration of Independence.

variants.question: In a first-past-the-post election, who wins the seat?
choices: The party with the most seats overall
The candidate chosen by the Speaker
The candidate with over half the votes
The candidate with the most votes
variants.explanation: A plurality is enough.

variants.question: Which system gives parties seats in proportion to the votes they receive?
variants.explanation: Proportional systems try to match seats to vote share.

variants.question: Which of these countries was one of the six founding members of the European Economic Community?
variants.explanation: Spain joined in 1986, Denmark and Ireland in 1973.

variants.question: The six founders were France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and which other country?
variants.explanation: Luxembourg completed the Inner Six.

variants.question: Which court, seated in The Hague, is the main judicial body of the United Nations?
choices: The European Court of Human Rights
variants.explanation: The ICJ settles disputes between states.

variants.question: Which court, sitting in Luxembourg, interprets European Union law?
choices: The European Court of Human Rights
The Court of Justice of the European Union
variants.explanation: It ensures that EU law is applied the same way in every member state.

variants.question: Which French document of 1789 proclaimed the rights of man and of the citizen?
choices: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
The Charter of the United Nations
variants.explanation: It was adopted by the National Constituent Assembly in August 1789.

variants.question: In which city was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted in 1948?
variants.explanation: The General Assembly met at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris.

variants.question: In economics, what is a recession?
choices: A significant fall in economic activity
variants.explanation: It is often defined as two consecutive quarters of falling GDP.

variants.question: What is the name of the severe global downturn that began in 1929?
variants.explanation: The Great Depression lasted through the 1930s.
